(basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 3,044 (3.8 apg) }} '''Ishmael Larry “Ish” Smith''' (born July 5, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is a professional scout for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. Smith holds the record of playing for the most NBA franchises, at 13. He won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2023.{{Cite web |title=DENVER NUGGETS WIN FIRST NBA CHAMPIONSHIP IN FRANCHISE HISTORY WITH 4-1 FINALS WIN OVER HEAT |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-win-first-nba-championship-in-franchise-history-with-4-1-finals-win-over-heat |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} ==High school career== Smith attended [[Central Cabarrus High School]] playing under Scott Brewer. He averaged 24.8 points and 9.8 assists per game as a senior and led Central Cabarrus to a 28–0 record and a MECA–6 Conference regular season and tournament title, which earned him the Meca–6 Conference Player of the Year in 2006, all-conference honors and being named Piedmont Player of the Year by ''[[The Charlotte Observer]]''{{'s}} (he also earned the last two accolades as a junior).{{Cite web |title=Ishmael Smith Bio |url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/smith_ishmael00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304191335/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/smith_ishmael00.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=October 27, 2010 |publisher=Wake Forest Demon Deacons Athletics}} When he graduated, he was ranked as the No. 28 [[point guard]] in the country according to Rivals.com while being rated by Scout.com as the No. 1 point guard and the No. 2 prospect nationally. ==College career== Smith played [[college basketball]] for [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], finishing second all-time for assists in school history. In his four years with the Deacons he had averages of 9.2 points, 5.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 121 games. He also stands as the only player in school history with 1,000 points (1,114) and 600 assists (612) in his career.{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2010 |title=Rockets Ink Ish |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets_sign_ismael_smith_2010_08_19.html |access-date=February 20, 2013 |website=NBA.com}} As a senior, Smith averaged 13.2 points, 6.0 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 1.68 steals. He was named Second-Team All-ACC and earned Second-Team All-District honors from the NABC. Smith also received the team's Murray Greason Award and Team Assists Leader award after finishing third in the ACC and seventh nationally in assists per game in 2009–10. ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2010–2011)=== After going undrafted on the [[2010 NBA draft]], Smith signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] on August 23, 2010. On January 17, 2011, he was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{Cite web |date=January 17, 2011 |title=Rockets assign Ishmael Smith to D-League |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=7039 |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=InsideHoops.com}} He was recalled by the Rockets on January 24, reassigned on February 1,{{Cite web |date=February 1, 2011 |title=Rockets re-assign Ishmael Smith to D-League |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=7109 |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=InsideHoops.com}} and recalled again on February 8 . === Memphis Grizzlies (2011) === On February 24, 2011, Smith was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with teammate [[Shane Battier]] in exchange for [[Hasheem Thabeet]], [[DeMarre Carroll]] and a future first-round draft pick.{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2011 |title=Rockets trade Shane Battier to Grizzlies; Hasheem Thabeet to Rockets |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=7242 |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=InsideHoops.com}} Smith made 15 appearances for the Grizzlies in the 2010–11 season after the trade, all off of the bench. On December 14, 2011, Smith was waived by the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |date=December 14, 2011 |title=Grizzlies waive Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-waive-ish-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} === Golden State Warriors (2011–2012) === On December 16, 2011, Smith was claimed off waivers by the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2011 |title=Warriors Awarded Guard Ish Smith Off Waivers |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_awarded_ish_smith_121611.html |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On December 28, he started for the Warriors in a win against the [[New York Knicks]] in place of the injured [[Stephen Curry]], scoring 11 points, with 6 rebounds and 4 assists.{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2011 |title=Monta Ellis, Warriors cruise by Knicks minus Stephen Curry |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=311228009 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Smith was later waived by the Warriors on January 13, 2012.{{Cite web |date=January 13, 2012 |title=Warriors Waive Guard Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ish_smith_waived_011312.html |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} === Orlando Magic (2012–2013) === On February 2, 2012, Smith signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2012 |title=Magic Sign Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_ishsmith_020212.html |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On August 15, 2012, he re-signed with the Magic.{{Cite web |date=August 15, 2012 |title=Magic Re-Sign Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-re-sign-ish-smith |access-date=December 29, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} === Milwaukee Bucks (2013) === On February 21, 2013, Smith was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with [[JJ Redick]] and [[Gustavo Ayón]] in exchange for [[Beno Udrih]], [[Doron Lamb]] and [[Tobias Harris]].{{Cite web |date=February 21, 2013 |title=Bucks Acquire JJ Redick, Gustavo Ayon and Ish Smith from Magic |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-jj-redick-gustavo-ayon-and-ish-smith-magic |access-date=February 24, 2013 |website=NBA.com}} ===Phoenix Suns (2013–2014)=== On August 29, 2013, Smith and [[Viacheslav Kravtsov]] were traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Caron Butler]].{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2013 |title=Suns Trade for Kravtsov, Smith From Bucks |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-trade-kravtsov-smith-bucks |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} In his third game with the Suns, Smith dished out a career-high 8 assists in a 104–98 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Smith matched his career-high in assists (along with 8 points, 2 rebounds and 3 steals) in a 116–100 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on January 4, 2014. Smith became one of only three Suns backups since the 1980s to collect at least two 8-assist games in less than 20 minutes of playing time in a single season; the others being [[Jeff Hornacek]] and [[Goran Dragić]].{{Cite web |date=January 6, 2014 |title=Quick Hits on Phoenix Suns signing Leandro Barbosa's impact on Christmas, Smith and Goodwin |url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2014/1/6/5279442/phoenix-suns-leandro-barbosas-archie-goodwin-dionte-christmas-ish-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=BrightSideOfTheSun.com}} On February 21, 2014, he scored a then-career-high 15 points in a 106–85 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489695 Spurs' nine-game road trip ends with loss to Ish Smith, Suns] On July 15, 2014, he was waived by the Suns.{{Cite web |date=July 15, 2014 |title=Suns Release Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-release-ish-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2014–2015)=== On July 19, 2014, Smith signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2014 |title=Rockets Add Depth to Roster with Signings |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-add-depth-roster-signings |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} However, he was waived by the Rockets on October 27 after appearing in seven preseason games.{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2014 |title=Rockets Waive Adrien, Clark, Covington, Richmond and Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-adrien-clark-covington-richmond-and-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On November 7, 2014, Smith signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Oklahoma City had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2014 |title=Thunder Signs Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_ishsmith_141107 |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} After the team's hardship exemption expired, Smith was kept on the roster as the Thunder released [[Sebastian Telfair]] instead.{{Cite news |date=November 26, 2014 |title=Thunder release Sebastian Telfair |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11945234 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2015)=== On February 19, 2015, Smith was traded, along with the rights to [[Latavious Williams]], cash considerations and draft considerations, to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for further draft considerations.{{Cite web |date=February 19, 2015 |title=Pelicans Acquire Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-ish-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} He was subsequently waived by the Pelicans later that day.{{Cite web |date=February 19, 2015 |title=Pelicans Waive Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-ish-smith |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On February 22, 2015, Smith signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite news |date=February 22, 2015 |title=Sixers Sign Ishmael Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150222-smith-signed |access-date=February 22, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} On March 2, 2015, he recorded career highs of 19 points and 9 assists in a loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |date=March 2, 2015 |title=Raptors top 76ers 114–103, snap 5-game losing streak |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150302/TORPHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151027144822/http://www.nba.com/games/20150302/TORPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 27, 2015 |access-date=September 25, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} The 76ers' offensive numbers demonstrably improved after acquiring Smith as their starting point guard,{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2015 |title=Analyzing The Sixers' Offensive Improvement Since The Trade Deadline |url=http://www.libertyballers.com/2015/3/25/8286481/analyzing-trends-since-the-trade-deadline |access-date=September 25, 2015 |website=LibertyBallers.com}} and [[Nerlens Noel]] referred to Smith as "the first true point guard I've ever really played with."{{Cite web |date=April 2, 2015 |title=Sixers' Noel has gotten a big assist from Smith's presence |url=http://articles.philly.com/2015-04-02/sports/60724415_1_nerlens-noel-ish-smith-michael-carter-williams |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616042902/http://articles.philly.com/2015-04-02/sports/60724415_1_nerlens-noel-ish-smith-michael-carter-williams |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 16, 2015 |access-date=September 25, 2015 |website=Philly.com}} On March 11 and April 1, he scored a career-high 23 points. He went on to average 12.0 points and 6.1 assists in 27.1 minutes per game for the 76ers in 2014–15, all career highs.{{Cite web |title=Ish Smith 2014–15 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithis01/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=September 25, 2015 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2015)=== On September 25, 2015, Smith signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2015 |title=Wizards Sign Five for Training Camp |url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/09/25/wizards-sign-five-for-training-camp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927204655/http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/09/25/wizards-sign-five-for-training-camp |archive-date=September 27, 2015 |access-date=September 25, 2015 |website=MonumentalNetwork.com}} However, he was later waived by the Wizards on October 24 after appearing in five preseason games.{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2015 |title=WIZARDS WAIVE FIVE |url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/10/24/wizards-waive-five |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025202356/http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/10/24/wizards-waive-five |archive-date=October 25, 2015 |access-date=October 24, 2015 |website=MonumentalNetwork.com}} On October 26, Smith was claimed off waivers by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2015 |title=Pelicans Sign Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-ish-smith |access-date=October 26, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=October 26, 2015 |title=Ish Smith Claimed Off Waivers By Pelicans |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/239663/Ish-Smith-Claimed-Off-Waivers-By-Pelicans |access-date=October 26, 2015 |website=RealGM.com}} and made his debut for the team the following day in the season opener. In 38 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded 17 points and 9 assists in a loss to the defending champion [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2015 |title=NBA MVP Curry scores 40 points, Warriors win opener |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/NOPGSW/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225100230/http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/NOPGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 25, 2015 |access-date=October 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On November 6, he recorded 8 points and a then-career-high 11 assists in a loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite news |date=November 6, 2015 |title=Korver helps Hawks win 6th straight, 121–115 over Pelicans |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/ATLNOP/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106214339/http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/ATLNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015 |access-date=November 6, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} Four days later, he recorded his first career double-double with 17 points and a career-high 12 assists in a 120–105 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], marking the Pelicans' first win of the season.{{Cite news |date=November 10, 2015 |title=Davis leaves with injured hip as Pelicans get first win |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/DALNOP/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005163757/http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/DALNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 5, 2016 |access-date=November 11, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} He broke his career high for assists for a third time on November 20, recording 17 points and 13 assists in a 104–90 win over the San Antonio Spurs.{{Cite news |date=November 20, 2015 |title=Davis' big game in return lifts Pelicans over Spurs, 104–90 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151120/SASNOP/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124063726/http://www.nba.com/games/20151120/SASNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 24, 2015 |access-date=November 20, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} ===Return to Philadelphia (2015–2016)=== [[File:Ish Smith 2016.jpg|thumb|Smith with the [[Detroit Pistons]] in 2016]] On December 24, 2015, Smith was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for two future second-round draft picks.{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2015 |title=Sixers Acquire Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-acquire-ish-smith |access-date=December 24, 2015 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} In his first game back for the 76ers two days later, he scored 14 points and helped the team record just their second win of the season with a 111–104 victory over the Phoenix Suns.{{Cite web |date=December 26, 2015 |title=Lowly 76ers beat Suns 111–104 for 2nd win of season |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151226/PHIPHX/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230214130/http://www.nba.com/games/20151226/PHIPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 30, 2015 |access-date=December 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On January 9, 2016, he scored a career-high 28 points in a loss to the Toronto Raptors. In that game, he scored 18 of the 76ers' 25 third-quarter points.{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2016 |title=Lowry, DeRozan lead Raptors to 108–95 win over 76ers |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160109/TORPHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109213511/http://www.nba.com/games/20160109/TORPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 9, 2016 |access-date=January 9, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On January 18, he recorded 16 points and a career-high 16 assists in a 119–113 double-overtime loss to the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2016 |title=Anthony ties it in regulation, Knicks beat 76ers in 2 OTs |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160118/PHINYK/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119135343/http://www.nba.com/games/20160118/PHINYK/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=January 18, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} ===Detroit Pistons (2016–2019)=== [[File:Ish Smith pass.jpg|thumb|Ish Smith in October 2019]] On July 8, 2016, Smith signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]],{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2016 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agents Ish Smith and Jon Leuer |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-ish-smith-and-jon-leuer |access-date=July 8, 2016 |website=NBA.com}} marking the tenth team he has played for in 7 seasons. On February 23, 2017, he had 15 assists off the bench in a 114–108 overtime win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]], becoming the first Detroit player with at least 15 assists in a reserve role since [[Kevin Porter (basketball, born 1950)|Kevin Porter]] had 19 in January 1977.{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2017 |title=Pistons rally from 18 down, beat Hornets 114–108 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900257 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 3, 2018, Smith scored 25 points in a 111–107 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. He went 11 of 14 from the field and finished three points shy of his career high—his previous season high was 19 points.{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2018 |title=Pistons win again with Griffin, 111–107 over Heat |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975522 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On October 20, 2018, he scored all 15 of his points in the second half, including the game-winning basket, in a 118–116 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2018 |title=Griffin, Smith lead Pistons over Bulls 118–116 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070714 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On January 14, 2019, he returned to action against the [[Utah Jazz]] after missing 19 games with a torn adductor muscle.{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2019 |title=Gobert grabs 25 rebounds as Jazz beat Pistons 100–94 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071324 |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} He aggravated the injury in his third game back.{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2019 |title=Hield beats buzzer, lifts Kings to 103–101 win over Pistons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071356 |access-date=January 19, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}} ===Washington Wizards (2019–2021)=== On July 9, 2019, Smith signed with the [[Washington Wizards]], and played his first game with the team on October 23, 2019, scoring 7 points.{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2019 |title=Wizards sign Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-ish-smith |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709192614/https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-ish-smith |archive-date=July 9, 2019 |access-date=July 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} This marked the 11th team that Smith played for in the previous eight seasons. ===Charlotte Hornets (2021–2022)=== On August 7, 2021, Smith signed with his hometown team, the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=August 7, 2021 |title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-ish-smith |website=NBA.com}} The signing marked Smith's record-tying 12th different NBA franchise, joining [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]], [[Chucky Brown]], [[Jim Jackson (basketball)|Jim Jackson]], [[Kevin Ollie]] and [[Tony Massenburg]] as the only players to play for 12 different NBA teams.{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2021 |title=Ish Smith reportedly agrees to deal with Hornets |url=https://www.yahoo.com/now/ish-smith-reportedly-agrees-deal-224119984.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAIiKlT91HMbf7xag4WgtoihVhBYkfta6OzSTIBqLpFD_lsq_ZyJtPU5HgeRzC-wRTrZXdClJ4UmSI7GFQG1178xndaIDUcM1FbRorm_ABukPSJBUQjQCezYVzQFt2bR0t7J4vZscG4sg4b64KjHxghacOeJR7Un44H59rYHk_F0P |website=yahoo.com }}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===Return to Washington (2022)=== On February 10, 2022, Smith was traded back to the Washington Wizards, alongside [[Vernon Carey Jr.]], in exchange for [[Montrezl Harrell]].{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Wizards acquire Smith and Carey Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-smith-carey-jr-021022 |website=NBA.com}} This marked his second stint in Washington. ===Denver Nuggets (2022–2023)=== On July 6, 2022, Smith was traded, alongside [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]], to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Monté Morris]] and [[Will Barton]].{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2022 |title=Nuggets Acquire Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Ish Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-kentavious-caldwell-pope-and-ish-smith/ |access-date=July 6, 2022 |website=nba.com}} On October 19, 2022, Smith made his team debut.
